title: Default extensions
description: Default reasoning with defaults that have no prerequisites (Poole systems): an extension is a maximal set of defaults consistent with the facts, and asking whether a query follows in some extension is Sigma-2-complete. The check has two ways to refute a candidate, a model in which the query is false or a model that satisfies one more default, each with its own relevant/1 rule. The sample is the Nixon diamond with a few more defaults.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: Facts, defaults and the query. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
clause(C) :- hard(C).
clause(C) :- default(C).
atom(A) :- pos(_,A).
atom(A) :- neg(_,A).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): sets of defaults that are consistent with the facts.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of defaults that is consistent with the hard knowledge.
% The model w/1 shows consistency; it is private to solver A (see the Abduction example).
{ on(D) } :- default(D).
{ w(A) } :- atom(A).
used(C) :- hard(C).
used(C) :- on(C).
:- used(C), not w(A) : pos(C,A); w(A) : neg(C,A).
#show on/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate. The check blames it when a counterexample does
% not depend on the candidate: then no candidate is a solution, and the clause "always
% must change" ends the search.
{ always }.
:- not always.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the chosen defaults.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a model that shows the query does not follow, or that one more default fits (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A model of the hard knowledge and the chosen defaults ...
{ m(A) } :- atom(A).
sat(C) :- pos(C,A), m(A).
sat(C) :- neg(C,A), not m(A).
:- hard(C), not sat(C).
:- on(D), not sat(D).
% ... is a counterexample in two cases:
% (1) the query is false in it: the chosen defaults do not entail the query;
open :- query(A), not m(A).
% (2) it satisfies a default that was left out: the set is not maximal.
fits(D) :- default(D), not on(D), sat(D).
more :- fits(D).
:- not open, not more.
#show m/1.

% In both cases the model refutes every set of defaults that are all true in it,
% so a default that is false in the model has to be chosen ...
relevant(on(D)) :- default(D), not sat(D).
% ... or, in case (2) only, the default that fits has to be chosen (the first, if several).
relevant(on(D)) :- not open, fits(D), not fits(E) : default(E), E < D.
% If the query is false although every default holds in the model, no set of defaults
% entails the query: blame the atom that is always true.
broken :- default(D), not sat(D).
relevant(always) :- open, not broken.

fragments.name: check_all_fits
fragments.description: The check of the variant all-fits: every default that fits is blamed, not only the first.
fragments.text:
% A model of the hard knowledge and the chosen defaults ...
{ m(A) } :- atom(A).
sat(C) :- pos(C,A), m(A).
sat(C) :- neg(C,A), not m(A).
:- hard(C), not sat(C).
:- on(D), not sat(D).
% ... is a counterexample in two cases:
% (1) the query is false in it: the chosen defaults do not entail the query;
open :- query(A), not m(A).
% (2) it satisfies a default that was left out: the set is not maximal.
fits(D) :- default(D), not on(D), sat(D).
more :- fits(D).
:- not open, not more.
#show m/1.

% In both cases the model refutes every set of defaults that are all true in it,
% so a default that is false in the model has to be chosen ...
relevant(on(D)) :- default(D), not sat(D).
% ... or, in case (2) only, one of the defaults that fit has to be chosen (all of them are
% named: weaker than naming the first one, still sound).
relevant(on(D)) :- not open, fits(D).
% If the query is false although every default holds in the model, no set of defaults
% entails the query: blame the atom that is always true.
broken :- default(D), not sat(D).
relevant(always) :- open, not broken.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

instances.facts:
% Facts and defaults in clause form: pos(C,A) / neg(C,A) as in a CNF.
% Hard knowledge: Nixon is a quaker and a republican; nobody is both a hawk and a pacifist.
pos(1,quaker).
pos(2,republican).
neg(3,hawk).  neg(3,pacifist).
hard(1..3).
% Defaults, each a clause that is assumed as long as this is consistent:
neg(d1,quaker).      pos(d1,pacifist).     % quakers are pacifists
neg(d2,republican).  pos(d2,hawk).         % republicans are hawks
neg(d3,hawk).        pos(d3,army).         % hawks support the army
neg(d4,pacifist).    neg(d4,army).         % pacifists do not
neg(d5,republican).  pos(d5,rich).         % republicans are rich
neg(d6,quaker).      neg(d6,rich).         % quakers are not
neg(d7,rich).        pos(d7,army).         % the rich support the army
default(d1;d2;d3;d4;d5;d6;d7).
% Does this follow in some extension?
query(army).

% Tweety is a penguin, penguins are birds and do not fly; birds fly by default.
% No extension makes Tweety fly.
pos(1,penguin).
neg(2,penguin). pos(2,bird).
neg(3,penguin). neg(3,flies).
hard(1..3).
neg(d1,bird). pos(d1,flies).               % birds fly
default(d1).
query(flies).

% Two defaults that exclude each other; each leads to the query by another default.
pos(1,student).
hard(1).
neg(d1,student). pos(d1,young).            % students are young
neg(d2,student). pos(d2,employed).         % students are employed
neg(d3,young).   neg(d3,employed).         % the young are not employed
neg(d4,employed). pos(d4,tax).             % the employed pay tax
neg(d5,young).   pos(d5,discount).         % the young get a discount
default(d1;d2;d3;d4;d5).
query(tax).

generators.name: dl-random
generators.description: Random hard literals and default rules: n atoms, h hard literals and k defaults "X implies (not) Y" between two random atoms (the conclusion positive with probability q/1000); the query is the conclusion of a random positive default.
generators.text:
% dl-random: atoms 1..n. The hard knowledge c(1..h) is h literals (true or false with
% probability 1/2, consistent); the defaults c(h+1..h+k) are rules "X implies Y" or
% "X implies not Y" (positive with probability q/1000) between two different random atoms.
% The query is the conclusion of a random positive default.
hard(c(1..h)).
default(c(h+1..h+k)).
fact(I,@int(1,n,atom,I),@flip(500,sign,I)) :- I = 1..h.
:- fact(I,A,1), fact(J,A,0).
pos(c(I),A) :- fact(I,A,1).
neg(c(I),A) :- fact(I,A,0).
rule(I,X,(X+@int(0,n-2,gap,I))\n+1,@flip(q,sign,I)) :- I = h+1..h+k, X = @int(1,n,premise,I).
neg(c(I),X) :- rule(I,X,Y,S).
pos(c(I),Y) :- rule(I,X,Y,1).
neg(c(I),Y) :- rule(I,X,Y,0).
query(Y) :- rule(I,X,Y,1), I = h + @int(1,k,query).
asked :- query(Y).
:- not asked.
#show hard/1.  #show default/1.  #show pos/2.  #show neg/2.  #show query/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: each refuted candidate is ruled out on its own.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.block(M))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--project"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Shape 1: A's own search, projected on the shown atoms (--project), so each candidate
# comes once whatever the hidden witness w/1.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three counterexamples per candidate, one clause each.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    XS = C.models(assume G(M), limit 3)
    if XS.size > 0:
        for X in XS: A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
